properties.chose: Taken as step 4 of the door plan Anthony agreed on 2026-10-01 ("I agree"): req:the-cli-describes-any-tool-with-its-full-schema-and-lessons.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea 5 in using_call.md (2026-10-01), for limitations 5 and 6:
- find_tools gives parameter NAMES only (query.rs ~853 collects the schema's property keys), so an agent learns types and required-ness from exit-2 refusals, "one round trip per mistake";
- the lessons a DesignRule or TemporalFact hangs on a tool (`steps`) ride that tool's description in tools/list (lessons.rs:230), which a `--call` agent never reads.

THE IDEA, in his words: "`--describe <tool>` (or `--call describe_tool`) would print the full input schema *and* the lessons `tools/list` would have appended. A `--list-tools` that dumps the whole served list as JSON would let an instructions generator pre-render a schema cheat-sheet."

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND VS CODE: req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue and req:conventions-ride-the-tool-not-only-the-skill put disciplines on the tool. Any door that skips tools/list loses them silently. As a served TOOL (describe_tool), it would also reach MCP clients that truncate long tool lists.

CHEAP: --call already builds the served list with lessons (tools_with_lessons, main.rs ~750), so printing one entry is small.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-01 — the CLI describes a tool in full, with its schema and lessons (step 4 of the door plan)
